# Section 010 Knowledge Check: Compute Placement And Sizing

<!-- TODO(build): generated by /astrona-course-generate-assessment against the objectives below. Scenario questions, no recall trivia. -->

## Coverage

- Set CPU and memory requests and limits on a container and read them back with kubectl get -o yaml
- Predict the QoS class (Guaranteed, Burstable, BestEffort) of a pod from its resources and confirm it in status.qosClass
- Diagnose a Pending pod whose requests do not fit any node from its FailedScheduling event
- Distinguish a container killed for exceeding its memory limit (OOMKilled) from a CPU-throttled container
- Compare a node's allocatable capacity with the sum of requests using kubectl describe node
- Locate the resources fields in the Kubernetes API reference and the resource management documentation
- Pin pods to labelled nodes with required node affinity and prefer nodes with preferred node affinity
- Reserve a node for one workload with a NoSchedule taint and a matching toleration
- Explain from pod events why a toleration alone does not move a pod onto a tainted node
- Keep replicas apart with pod anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname
- Spread replicas evenly across zones with a topology spread constraint and read the effect of maxSkew and whenUnsatisfiable
- Diagnose a Pending pod caused by an unmatched affinity rule or an untolerated taint from its FailedScheduling message
